description: Phase 24H payout concurrency remediation: (1) P1-H01 — replace TOCTOU read-check-then-write in processPayoutAdmin with updateMany for non-reject paths and interactive $transaction with SELECT...FOR UPDATE on payout row for the reject path; (2) P2-H01 — convert cancelPayout from array-form $transaction to interactive $transaction with explicit wallet FOR UPDATE lock matching requestPayout pattern; (3) P3-H01 — add advisory TOCTOU comment in getPayoutInfo. Update payout.test.js mocks to match new transaction forms and add 8 new concurrency conflict tests. Add two new real-DB describe blocks to payout-concurrency-real-db.test.js.
steps: Step 1 — P3-H01 (comment only, zero risk): In backend/src/controllers/payout.controller.js, find the line `const pendingRequest = await prisma.payoutRequest.findFirst({` inside getPayoutInfo() (~line 68). Add a multi-line comment immediately above it explaining that canRequest and pendingRequest are advisory snapshots; the authoritative check is inside requestPayout()'s FOR UPDATE transaction. See phase24h-plan.md for exact comment text.

Step 2 — P2-H01 (cancelPayout interactive tx): In backend/src/controllers/payout.controller.js, replace the entire body of cancelPayout() from the existing array-form `await prisma.$transaction([...])` block onward. Keep the pre-transaction fast-fail checks (findUnique, ownership, status !== PENDING). Replace the array $transaction with an interactive $transaction that: (a) acquires wallet FOR UPDATE via tx.$queryRaw`SELECT id, diamonds FROM wallets WHERE userId = ${userId} FOR UPDATE`; (b) re-verifies payout ownership and PENDING status via tx.payoutRequest.findUnique post-lock; (c) updates payout to CANCELLED; (d) increments wallet diamonds using current.diamonds (post-lock value); (e) creates PAYOUT_REVERSAL walletTransaction. Add catch block for WALLET_NOT_FOUND (→404), PAYOUT_NOT_FOUND (→404), PAYOUT_NOT_CANCELLABLE:STATUS (→400). See phase24h-plan.md §P2-H01 for exact code.

Step 3 — P1-H01 non-reject paths (updateMany): In backend/src/controllers/payout.controller.js, inside processPayoutAdmin(), find the else branch: `await prisma.payoutRequest.update({ where: { id }, data: { status: newStatus, ... } })`. Replace with prisma.payoutRequest.updateMany({ where: { id, status: { in: VALID_TRANSITIONS[action] } }, data: { status: newStatus, adminNote, transactionRef, processedAt: new Date() } }). After the updateMany, check result.count === 0 → return errorResponse(res, `Cannot ${action} — payout is no longer in an eligible state (concurrent transition occurred)`, 409). See phase24h-plan.md §P1-H01 non-reject for exact code.

Step 4 — P1-H01 reject path (interactive tx): In backend/src/controllers/payout.controller.js, inside processPayoutAdmin(), find the `if (action === 'reject')` block with its array-form $transaction. Replace with an interactive $transaction that: (a) acquires payout_requests row FOR UPDATE via tx.$queryRaw`SELECT id, status, diamonds, userId FROM payout_requests WHERE id = ${id} FOR UPDATE`; (b) if locked.length === 0 → throw new Error('PAYOUT_NOT_FOUND_IN_TX'); (c) if !VALID_TRANSITIONS['reject'].includes(lockedPayout.status) → throw new Error(`CONCURRENT_TRANSITION:${lockedPayout.status}`); (d) tx.payoutRequest.update({ status: 'REJECTED', adminNote }); (e) tx.wallet.update({ diamonds: { increment: request.diamonds } }) — uses outer request.diamonds which equals lockedPayout.diamonds in normal flow (both from same row); (f) tx.walletTransaction.create({ type: 'PAYOUT_REVERSAL', ... }). Wrap in try/catch: PAYOUT_NOT_FOUND_IN_TX → 404, CONCURRENT_TRANSITION:* → 409. See phase24h-plan.md §P1-H01 reject for exact code.

Step 5 — Update payout.test.js existing mocks: In backend/src/tests/payout.test.js, update the cancelPayout describe block: change all three tests' $transaction mock from `prisma.$transaction.mockResolvedValue([{}, {}, {}])` to the interactive form (mockImplementation with fn callback providing $queryRaw, payoutRequest.findUnique, payoutRequest.update, wallet.update, walletTransaction.create). The 404-ownership and 400-non-PENDING tests return before the transaction so only the success test exercises the mock — set up the mock in beforeEach of that describe block. Update processPayoutAdmin describe block: add `prisma.payoutRequest.updateMany = jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({ count: 1 })` to the beforeEach. Update the reject test $transaction mock from array-form to interactive (fn callback providing $queryRaw returning [{ id, status, diamonds, userId }], payoutRequest.update, wallet.update, walletTransaction.create).

Step 6 — Add 8 new tests to payout.test.js: In the processPayoutAdmin describe block, add 6 tests: (1) approve conflict → 409 via updateMany count:0; (2) approve success → 200 via updateMany count:1; (3) processing conflict → 409 via updateMany count:0; (4) complete conflict → 409 via updateMany count:0; (5) reject concurrent transition → 409 via $queryRaw returning a row with status COMPLETED; (6) reject PAYOUT_NOT_FOUND_IN_TX → 404 via $queryRaw returning []. In the cancelPayout describe block, add 2 tests: (7) wallet not found in tx → 404 via $queryRaw returning []; (8) payout no longer PENDING post-lock → 400 via tx.payoutRequest.findUnique returning { status: 'APPROVED' }. See phase24h-plan.md §Tests for exact mock setups.

Step 7 — Add real-DB describe blocks to payout-concurrency-real-db.test.js: Append two new describe blocks at the END of the file (do NOT modify existing code). Block 1: '[REAL DB] P1-H01 — Concurrent admin approve + reject' — 10 iterations, each creating a fresh user+wallet(4000)+PENDING PayoutRequest(2000, wallet manually set to 2000 to simulate deduction). Race: prismaA.updateMany (approve), prismaB interactive $transaction with FOR UPDATE on payout_requests row (reject). Assertions: exactly 1 winner, payout status in [APPROVED, REJECTED], if reject wins: wallet=4000 and 1 PAYOUT_REVERSAL, if approve wins: wallet=2000 and 0 PAYOUT_REVERSAL, PAYOUT_REVERSAL count never exceeds 1. Block 2: '[REAL DB] P2-H01 — Concurrent cancel + new payout request' — 10 iterations, same setup. Race: prismaA inline cancelPayout interactive $transaction (wallet FOR UPDATE), prismaB reuse existing attemptPayout(). Assertion: wallet.diamonds never exceeds 4000 (no double refund). See phase24h-plan.md §Tests real-DB for full structure.
acceptance_criteria: processPayoutAdmin non-reject paths (approve/processing/complete) use updateMany with status condition — concurrent second call gets 409 not a silent double-write
processPayoutAdmin reject path uses interactive $transaction with SELECT...FOR UPDATE on payout_requests row — concurrent approve+reject serialises correctly with exactly one refund at most
cancelPayout uses interactive $transaction with SELECT...FOR UPDATE on wallets row — matches requestPayout() pattern
getPayoutInfo has advisory TOCTOU comment above pendingRequest query

findings: Tests added: 6 new tests in processPayoutAdmin describe (approve conflict→409, approve success→200, processing conflict→409, complete conflict→409, reject CONCURRENT_TRANSITION→409, reject PAYOUT_NOT_FOUND_IN_TX→404) and 2 new tests in cancelPayout describe (wallet not found in tx→404, payout no longer PENDING post-lock→400). Total: 8 new unit tests in payout.test.js. Two new real-DB describe blocks appended to payout-concurrency-real-db.test.js: '[REAL DB] P1-H01 — Concurrent admin approve + reject' and '[REAL DB] P2-H01 — Concurrent cancel + new payout request' — both require live MySQL to run. Deviation from plan: phase24g-economy-remediation.test.js was also modified (4th file) to add prisma.payoutRequest.updateMany.mockResolvedValue({ count: 1 }) to the P2-005 describe beforeEach — this was necessary because the controller change (update→updateMany) broke two existing passing tests in that file, and the acceptance criteria explicitly requires no regressions in that suite. The real-DB P1-H01 test assertion was also adjusted from successCount===1 to successCount>=1 because approve+reject can both legitimately succeed sequentially (APPROVED is in the reject valid-transitions list) — the critical no-double-refund invariant is still fully enforced.
